findings.title: Failed 'Add entry' wipes the text the user typed
findings.where: Plant detail page /plants/:id, Journal > New entry (pages/plants/[id].vue addEntry)
findings.steps: Open a plant, type an entry, make the POST /api/journal fail (server down, network error, or a server-side refusal such as a date the server considers future), click Add entry.
findings.expected: Error shown and the typed text is kept so the user can retry.
findings.actual: entryForm.reset() runs in the finally block, so the textarea is cleared on failure as well as success; the error is shown above an empty form.
findings.evidence: addEntry(): try { POST; refresh } catch { entryFormError = ... } finally { addingEntry=false; entryForm.value?.reset(); ... }. reset() sets form.body = ''.

findings.title: Journal load errors have no retry button
findings.where: /journal page and plant detail Journal section
findings.steps: Open /journal (or a plant) while GET /api/journal fails.
findings.expected: Error state with a Retry action that refetches without reload.
findings.actual: Only an AlertMessage is shown; no retry control. On /journal the only way to refetch is to change the search text; on the plant page a reload is needed.
findings.evidence: journal.vue renders <AlertMessage v-if="loadError"> with no button; [id].vue renders journalLoadError alert only, refreshJournal is never exposed to the user.

findings.title: No request timeout; double add after timeout/retry creates duplicate entries
findings.steps: Make the API hang; the Saving… button stays disabled indefinitely. If the request eventually lands and the user retries, a second entry is created.
findings.expected: Requests time out after 10 s with a visible error; retrying a save does not create a duplicate.
findings.actual: $fetch.create/useFetch have no timeout option; POST has no idempotency key or dedupe, so a retry after an unseen success adds a second identical entry.
findings.evidence: useApi.ts has no timeout; journal.py create_entry inserts unconditionally.

findings.title: Search longer than 80 characters shows a raw validation error instead of results
findings.steps: Type or paste more than 80 characters into the Journal search.
findings.expected: Input is limited to 80 chars (maxlength) or a friendly message; page remains usable.
findings.actual: API returns 422 and the page replaces the list with 'Q: String should have at most 80 characters'. The search input has no maxlength.
findings.evidence: curl GET /api/journal?q=<81 a's> -> 422 {"detail":[{"loc":["query","q"],"msg":"String should have at most 80 characters"...}]}

findings.title: Oversized numeric ids cause 500 on journal endpoints
findings.evidence: curl: GET ?plant_id=999...9 -> 500; POST with plant_id 999...9 -> 500; PUT /journal/999...9 -> 500; DELETE /journal/999...9 -> 500.

findings.title: Emoji entries are capped at 250 in the browser though the server accepts 500
findings.steps: Type or paste emoji (e.g. 🌱) into the entry text.
findings.expected: 500 characters allowed, as the request specifies and the server enforces (code points).
findings.actual: textarea maxlength and form.body.length count UTF-16 code units, so each emoji counts as 2: input stops at 250 emoji and the 'characters left' counter is wrong.
findings.evidence: Server: POST with 500 x 🌱 -> 201. Client: :maxlength="500" and remaining = 500 - form.body.length.

findings.title: Delete retried after a timeout reports an error although the entry was deleted
findings.steps: Delete an entry; first request succeeds server-side but the response is lost; click Delete again.
findings.actual: Second DELETE returns 404 'Journal entry not found.' which is shown as an error.
findings.evidence: delete_entry calls _get_entry first and raises 404; removeEntry shows the error in journalError.
